mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for four consecutive weeks (-16.1 to -29.1), reflecting entrenched reduction in discretionary outings. This momentum persists via habit formation and supply-side closures, so the trend continues downward over the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell monotonically from -16.1 to -29.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds (is less negative than) the mean over the last 28 days, indicating momentum broke.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES exceeding 10 points combined with a rise in RESIDENTIAL signals newly tightened stay-at-home policy enforcement, which mechanically curtails retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises more than 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -16.7 to -19.9 and from -7.7 to -16.7 in prior weeks while RESIDENTIAL rose from 8.4 to 12.3 to 13.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stabilizes over the two weeks following a qualifying WORKPLACES drop and RESIDENTIAL rise, despite the trigger firing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly compound to reduce incidental retail stops that normally piggyback on commuting trips, producing a larger drop in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -15.1 to -27.0 and WORKPLACES fell from -5.3 to -19.9 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no larger than the decline predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES individually in a linear additive model, i.e., no measurable interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in PARKS mobility reflects seasonal cooling that reduces outdoor-linked recreational trips; because many retail-and-recreation visits are bundled with outdoor outings, continued PARKS weakness under a seasonal-cooling regime drags RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -18.0 to -23.7 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves or holds steady over the next 28 days despite continued PARKS decline, indicating no seasonal linkage.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility dropped sharply in the last observed week (26.1 to 19.4) after three weeks of sustained elevation, suggesting saturation of essential-shopping stockpiling behavior. This saturation historically precedes a mean-reversion stabilization in overall discretionary mobility, nudging RETAIL_REC upward in the near term.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 5 points week-on-week after at least two prior weeks of rising or flat values
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 24.3 to 26.0 to 26.1 then fell to 19.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the week immediately following the GROCERY_PHARM drop, with no uptick observed.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen every week for four consecutive weeks, indicating a continuous tightening of stay-at-home policy compliance. This sustained trend independently and continuously suppresses RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as households persist in reduced outside activity.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 7.0 to 13.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days is equal to or higher than the prior 14-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise.

mechanism_narrative: Joint weekly declines in TRANSIT and PARKS indicate a broad behavioral retreat from all forms of out-of-home activity, not just commuting or outdoor leisure individually. This combined retreat compounds to further suppress retail-and-recreation visits over the next two weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -15.1 to -27.0 and PARKS fell from -18.0 to -23.7 concurrently
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline matches or is smaller than the sum of effects predicted by TRANSIT and PARKS independently, showing no compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a one-week dip, GROCERY_PHARM remains substantially elevated above baseline (19.4 vs typical 0), consistent with ongoing stockpiling behavior characteristic of a tightening-restrictions regime. Under this regime, elevated essential-goods demand crowds out discretionary retail trips, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remains at 19.4 (well above zero baseline) even after its recent dip
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated above 15, contradicting the crowding-out mechanism.
